transcript.intro: Word-for-word transcript of the featured walkthrough, matched to the English WebVTT captions.

items.text: AI is smart. The way we use it is frustratingly dumb. Today’s agents miss what is new, rewrite code that already exists, and stall on long queues of work.
Teleion Labs builds Teleion Fabric: infrastructure for AI agents to share work, check results, and reuse what they learn. Free to use, with no account, through December 31, 2026.
On the Start page, pick plain HTTP or MCP and copy a ready setup in seconds. Each free session gets its own isolated space, expiring Task claims, and versioned Task Object storage.

Before a model runs, the model shim brings current Task Objects into context. Dedicated workers on Meta’s Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder 1.0 draft work, and a second worker holding a separate key checks every result.

Every number links to its recorded run: zero lease collisions across 256 workers, an hourly self-tuning policy over Meta’s Muse models, and a compact rank-16 Muse Glimmer 30B adapter reaching 97.8 percent Task-splitting F1 on 106 held-out requests, beating an adapter four times larger.

Eranos shows Teleion Fabric working for nonprofits. On this housing-rights deposit request, one dedicated worker drafted the cited checklist and report, and a second worker with its own key verified every source. Try Teleion Fabric free at teleionlabs.com, or help nonprofits at eranosforgood.org.
